title: Flawless
body:
Probably the best, and most intuitive reminder app I have ever used. 

My entire experience so far with this app has been nothing short of perfect. There are a few features that I don’t use, such as the ‘boards’, but unlike so many of the other apps I’ve tried, I don’t feel I need to, as you can really use this in whatever way you want, rather than one prescribed way of doing it.

The widgets are fantastic and have a lot of flexibility, letting you quickly see upcoming tasks, anything that’s overdue, and easily add more entries. 

Assigning dates, priorities, and lists to each reminder is super simple, just being able to press and hold on it, and it even picks up phrases to automatically assign them. 

So far I’ve felt that the free tier offers enough for just myself, and the app never gets in your face trying to get you to upgrade. No popups, no “limited time” discounts, just a small banner at the top of the ‘browse’ page. 

10/10

title: Amazing for Neurodiverse individuals, particularly those struggling with executive function.
body:
The app is extremely comprehensive. However, it doesn’t force you to be. Due to the extensive, layered customise ability it allows truly for customisation to one’s personal desires, needs and cognitive profile. If you want to work through one project and not have any sub projects that is completely possible. If you just want to have one task list with no sub tasks, that is completely possible also. In addition to these layered and customisability. 

Conversely, to an extent like myself, I for years had longed for a greater depth and ability too further Breakdown and chunk tasks into smaller steps and ultimately customise My to-do list and planner. This is because ultimately. Especially when on the autistic spectrum, one has a tendency to systemise and focus on the small details write things down into constituents and therefore this is often a way that works for people with this sort of Neuro type as look at the task as a whole does not actually equal one step. 

So the ability to create projects and soft projects and add people. The ability to filter and label is extensive. Unlike other to-do list apps, you decide how many reminders you want they don’t give you a time you can add whatever time you want and there’s many reminders as you want event, it’s very easy to have a repeating task to the exact amount of days that suits you. 

Although this is the first planner/to-do list I paid for (£4.99), considering the struggles with productivity, engaging in activities of daily living, managing executive dysfunction and other non-neuro diverse conditions with a physical & cognitive-affective perceived aetiology

body:
I’ve decided to rerate to 4 star from 5.

My main issue is the lack of colour.

I cannot see at an instant my most important tasks of the day. I know, as previously mentioned, I can filter on Priority 1s but surely it would be far better to see at an instant the priority ones - Yes there is a hardly noticeable little coloured dot before the event, but its not easy to see at an instant.

Id like to see entries in a list that can have a coloured background when they are urgent and generally a splash of colour elsewhere too

Its a very boring looking interface to be honest. Pretty useful, but could definitely do with a face lift to make it more aesthetically pleasing.

Just my thoughts for what its worth

I am now trying to move over to Outlook, purely because of the colour coded entries I can employ.

The following I would like to see very much which I commented on a long time ago (The last paragraph) Its not easy to spot a little purple or red circle as a high priority item (Yes I know you can filter, but to have a fully coloured panel would make life so much easier) Otherwise an excellent program One more thing which would improve too which is to rename Projects to Sections or something like that. I have so called ‘Projects’ like Birthdays and Important Historical Events which are definitely not Projects Maybe not Sections, but something other than Projects which is just not correct If you'd like to get in touch with me, please email me -Thanks But Id like to see more prominent methods to see my most important tasks - maybe colour coded text or colour coded panels like you could use like outlook or gmail where you can see at an instant or glance what your priorities are - The flags are a little too small and inconspicuous for my likening Just my opinion - But overall very good

title: Redesign went against productivity
body:
I considered this as a 6-star app up till the design update. I am usually up for redesigns, however, not when features and the productivity goes down with it.

Excessive white spaces and line heights so I can see a lot less data on the screen and have to scroll a lot.

Removing the colours from the checkboxes, which indicated the relevant projects in a glimpse, now I need to look at a task then look towards the other side to see what project.. Not the end of the world but its distracts the previous smooth flow.

The mac layout became even worse. People usually working with the task more not on the sidebar, and now the add task button moved out of a convenient, close click to the sidebar..

Search needs an additional click instead of just type..

I'd like to say something positive about the update as well but unfortunately nothing comes to my mind so far - maybe because of the annoyance caused by this change. The mobile nav at the bottom maybe. Happy with that part.

Hopefully you'll address these newly created inconveniences, eg configurable new task button location (on mac the bar is still there, you just removed the useful buttons..), the coloured checkboxes could also be optional, and a 'compact view' theme or something would be much appreciated.

body:

It’s early days for me using To Doist but already it feels like a game changer. body: It does one thing(To-do list) but does it really well. Pros: 1. Keywords recognition in the title of the task. 6. No Share menu (impossible to send data to other apps)

If you’re a basic user, it might work for you, but you will find lots of people who outgrow Todoist very quickly.

title: Good app with some frustrating aspects
body:
I've tried Todoist a few times and have felt disappointed and frustrated each time. Of course all to-do apps differ and won't suit everyone's needs, but it behaves in some inexplicably annoying ways.

What I like: good natural language entry. Tasks can repeat on completion (e.g. every 2 months after you last did it) and on weekdays only (e.g. every 1st weekday of the month). Nested projects. You can add attachments to projects as well as tasks (in the premium version). Custom filters. Markdown support. Ability to pin favourite projects, labels and filters.

What I don’t like: you can’t make repeating checklists ie one repeating task with subtasks as when the task comes back the subtasks don’t regenerate - you have to manually uncomplete them. This is unfathomable. I emailed support who suggested project templates as a workaround - so apparently they don’t understand how people use repeating checklists which is beyond baffling. 

While you can name a custom filter in the sidebar, the filter query string appears on the page instead of being able to give it a 'friendly' name (I want to see 'Urgent work tasks' as the page title, not a line of gobbledegook). 

There are no badge options beyond on/off, whereas other apps let you choose whether to show all today's tasks, or just overdue ones, or today and the inbox, etc - I like to keep my badge notifications to a meaningful minimum, and found it really frustrating being unable to choose.

You can't pick different themes for when your system is in light or dark mode - you can only pick one for all the time. The daily agenda is a nice idea but it's only available at 9am and, newsflash, NOT EVERYONE STARTS THEIR DAY AT 9 (that’s way too late to be any use to me). 

No adding notes to tasks, only time-stamped comments which are NOT THE SAME AS NOTES (some apps have both) and markdown doesn't work in them - this is just unfathomable, why would you have markdown support and not allow people to write comments using it?

Calendar sync only works with Google and is focused on adding tasks to your calendar - I want to see my calendar events in my task manager not vice versa, from multiple calendars, so this doesn't work for me at all. 

And no batch adding (ie paste in multiple tasks from the clipboard) on mobile, only on the web.

Some of these complaints are just individual preferences - apps will suit some people and not others. But some of them represent bad UX decisions, and in some cases a failure to offer options for a variety of people - I noticed quite a few areas where other apps would offer multiple options but Todoist only does it one way. 

Task managers should make you feel like everything is sorted and in hand, so you're not stressed. For me, the above issues made this impossible with Todoist, so I've given up on it.

My one critique of this amazing app would be please give us the ability to set a do and a due date separately. I usually have a due date to complete a task and usually that doesn’t tie in with my do date (always before). Having the ability to set both would stop me having to refer to other notes to see when something is due after I have completed it. If I had access to both right there, I could create my “submit this work” task as I am ticking off the completion of said task.

body:

The new subtasks functionality works well (was clearly a missing piece before its introduction).  

I follow (perhaps loosely) the principles of GTD (read the book if you’ve never heard of it) and I can fit most of this within the functionality of Todoist.

Downsides - it takes a little bit of time to set up and perhaps a little more time to maintain than others (Wunderlist used to be a bit easier but is no longer supported and has been replace by Microsoft’s dreadful todo app).  That said, it’s worth the investment to stay on top of things and be more productive in the moment.

Overall, highly recommended and I’ve not found a better To do app out there (and I’ve tried a few).

title: Clever, joined up, does the job.
body:
I researched and tested to find a task management app that offered every capability on my list and out of a huge range this was the only one I found that did it all. 
It works equally well on my Windows 10 laptop and iPhone. Writes to my Calendar. Syncs immediately with no glitches. Adding tasks is a very simple process. Allows you to organise everything however you want with the same process: create complex tasks within tasks within tasks with notes and reminders and recurrences if you want or just simple flat lists. All using the same clear tool set. Quite glad I found it. 
Also liked the date recognition as you type so no tedious selecting from drop downs. Liked the filters had Boolean capabilities so you could be very sophisticated if you wanted. Liked how shared lists make it painless to keep everyone up to date instantly and has a nice commenting function for little discussions. 
Liked the knowledge base. It's all very well thought out. 
The basic version offers what I needed too but I paid the subscription as I was genuinely impressed. However I'm hoping this means there's active development and new features will keep it interesting. (Be good to have some automation with labels and priorities as they change overtime for example.) Lost a star because although it's not that important to be able to personalise with colours and formatting or customise or replace the inbox etc. but it would be a better if you could.

- Saving smart searches nowadays shouldn't be hard to offer as a feature

title: Pretty but flawed
body: Todoist works well in many respects - it looks great with a lovely clean aesthetic, it is platform agnostic so if you need to switch between mobile, Mac & PC your tasks are available - if you fork out @€28 per year you get lots of extra functionality, including file uploads, mail tasks into the app and funky coloured labels. Not bad. *Unfortunately* one of its biggest failings (and the deal-killer for many busy people, including me) is the startling omission of start dates - I.e. When you actually need to start a task or project (follow on, stage sequential etc.) and the ability to hide tasks until they need to be seen - this is imperative in most business or project management workflows; instead you have do a convoluted series of kludges involving flags or due dates or labels and filters, none of which are satisfactory or conducive to good productivity. It's a shame as  it's an often requested feature that the developers seem bent on ignoring. For this reason I've decided not to re-subscribe Todoist for business and am moving my team to pastures new - hopefully the Devs will add the feature in the future and my business will consider a return. Fingers crossed.

Natural language support is good. But you can't specify the project, so feels half baked and clunky the way you have to select the project afterwards.

The alert sound is just the default iOS notification sound, so when you hear it the sound could be from anything (you can't tell if it's a Todoist alert, answerphone message or whatever).
Also, it adds the [project name] at the end of the notification, which looks ugly. 

I don't mind paying a premium, but it seems the developers want to spend time working on the new logo, rather than making the app more streamlined and easier to use.

title: Fantastic but needs tweaks
body:
Still reliant on Todoist as my task management app & find it invaluable. 

I like the new branding (apart from the lack of contrast in some "themes") and I think the new logo/icon is strong.

I just wish they'd put all that development time into fixing some longstanding bugs/limitations. Many of the problems (some in my earlier reviews, below) are not fixed. A new icon can't fix bugs.

But somehow overall it's still brilliant...

-----

- It can freeze when there are too many tasks due.

- I wish the developers would communicate more thoroughly with users about changes & updates, both when they occur, and also in response to requests made on the forum. 

- There are still some major details which make the desktop versions in particular harder to use than they should be (i.e. no "select all" & filters giving incorrect results).

Still the best task system I've used, but frustrating nonetheless.

Previous reviews:
The new bugs are getting in my way. They all relate to tasks recurring incorrectly which is a vital aspect of a task management app.
Previous review:
I'm really impressed with the update to version 10, especially being able to select several tasks to edit at once on the iPhone.
But a couple of bugs have crept in: 
*Recurring tasks with a set time frequently don't appear in the correct place in the list.
*Tasks set to recur starting on a set date don't repeat correctly when completed.
Fantastic app though, and great to see big updates.
Previous review:
Finally a productivity app which really does improve my productivity.
I've switched all my tasks over to Todoist. It's a great, stable, multi-platform, app which keeps improving with very active, helpful developers. 
A couple of features I'd like added are: 
•Increased range of search-syntax to include specific projects, locations, etc.
•More swipe actions from task list.
•A way to remove due date from several tasks at once.
I'm looking forward to future app updates to see how it improves.

title: Incredibly useful!
body:
I've just started revising for my A2-level exams and have been looking for something to mark off my progress as I go through each individual component in the courses. I am also studying computing, for which I have to produce a piece of coursework.
Both involve numerous layers of tasks, subtasks, sub-subtasks etc. Nothing I found was good enough. Nothing allowed me to break down these tasks as much as I needed in order to have small, easily actionable tasks organised correctly.
Until I found Todoist, that is.
Tasks can be nested seemingly endlessly. It has an inbox for shoving tasks in before arranging at a later date, should you want, and you can create projects to store related tasks in. It features task recursion, with natural language understanding.
Todoist is helping me become more productive.
It also looks great, which absolutely helps. I can't recommend Todoist enough!

3) unable to filter by project for premium users (which makes premium pointless)

title: Regretting going premium - try Any.do
body:
At first, this app seemed perfect, multi platform, clean interface etc.  I had used Astrid and this looked and felt just as good. Sadly after paying for premium services, I spotted the following pretty major problems: 

1) Crashes if used with XCon

2) You can email asks in, but there's no way to email out. For £20, this is a pretty basic and important facility. I *need* to be able to send out email reminders containing the task and notes to people that don't use the app. Astrid and Orchestra both do/did this. 

3) No data export function/option, once your data is in, it's not getting out again :/ 

4) No search!?! You cannot search your tasks in iOS apps. Again a pretty basic ask. You can search in the PC/Mac web interface, but not in mobile apps, again a pretty major flaw for me. 

I way I'd read my review before spending £20, hence writing this for others. If the above doesn't bother you, then it's a pretty reasonable GTD interface.
